text:
Philip Rubin earned his BA in psychology and linguistics from Brandeis University in 1971, followed by a PhD in experimental psychology from the University of Connecticut in 1975, supervised by several individuals including Michael Turvey.
His research focuses across computational, engineering, linguistic, physiological, and psychological domains, particularly studying embodied cognition and the biological basis of speech and language. Rubin is recognized for his work on articulatory synthesis (modeling speech production physiology and acoustics), speech perception, and signal processing. Key contributions include designing ASY (Haskins articulatory synthesis program) and SWS (Haskins sinewave synthesis program), and designing the HADES signal processing system and the SPIEL programming language (a predecessor to MATLAB). He also made theoretical contributions to speech, focusing on dynamical systems and an event-based approach to speech production, and was instrumental in science administration and policy advocacy, including roles at the National Science Foundation (NSF) and the Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) in the White House.
